tool_applicability_notes: The registered global tool inventory still has no independently verified PDE-specific tool whose preconditions witness a direct transfer to finite-I Navier–Stokes blow-up classification.

Positive source patterns were nevertheless reviewed directly: Albritton–Barker compactness/persistence, Gallagher–Koch–Planchon critical elements, and Pineau–Vicol weighted enstrophy. They remain source methods, not registered success-tool authority for this atom.
failure_reuse_notes: F-C023-SCALAR-COLLAPSE is reused only as a warning that one critical scalar bound can erase orbit-class information; applicability here is witnessed by the distinction between fixed, periodic/RDSS, and general renormalized trajectories sharing Type-I scaling.

F-NS-B1a-C001-PRESSURE-SUMMABILITY applies to attempts that reconstruct global pressure control from unsummed far-field shells; it does not blacklist Pineau–Vicol's separately assumed fixed-annulus pressure L-infinity bound.

F-NS-B1a1-ABSOLUTE-LOCAL-ENERGY-SCALE-CURRENCY applies because a near-stationary-slice extraction cannot be justified by summing absolute critical shell costs across infinitely many scales. Signed/telescoping or genuinely monotone controls remain live.
unresolved_warnings: Pineau–Vicol v2 is a new primary-source input and must be cited by exact version/date; v1 lacked the local Theorem 1.9 result.
No implication finite I -> pointwise Type-I velocity bound is source-bound.
No implication pressure D -> fixed-annulus L-infinity pressure is source-bound.
